title: I made a defense game where taking more work can sink your construction crew. The free Steam demo is out.
author: DDANSAP
selftext:
Buy another excavator, merge what you have, or leave your cash in a fictional market and hope you can sell before the site overflows? That's the choice in Industrial Luck Defense, my solo construction defense game. The free English-language Windows demo is now playable on Steam.



You start with short company jobs, then open replayable EASY/NORMAL sites. Draws are random, but placement, merging and when to take extra work are decisions you make. Standard runs reach 50 waves, followed by an optional construction challenge using the crew you built.



A development lesson since my earlier input-bug post: progression can hide the fun if you lock too much. We initially held merging back with the more complicated systems. That was the wrong split. Procurement, placement, selling and merging now work from the first job; investment and tuning open later. We also cut repeated explanations instead of adding another tutorial popup.



I use ChatGPT/Codex and AI-assisted art and audio, with human direction and actual packaged-game checks. AI helped implement the changes, but deciding which systems belonged in the first job—and finding that visible buttons could still be blocked by another panel—needed testing the flow, not just asking whether the code passed.
